title: Why Escalator Stairs Vanish Into the Floor
sources: HowStuffWorks 'How Escalators Work' (science.howstuffworks.com/transport/engines-equipment/escalator.htm, 'Steppin' Out') / Wonderopolis 'How Do Escalators Work?' / Designing Buildings Wiki 'Escalator components' / Encyclopedia.com 'Escalator': each step has two pairs of wheels; the front wheels ride on one track (pulled by the drive chain), the rear wheels on a second track; the tracks' spacing keeps each step level; on the incline the tracks are offset so the steps form stairs; near the top and bottom the two tracks level off so the steps flatten into a platform; the steps loop around a drive gear and return upside down underneath; steps have cleats/grooves that mesh with the comb plate's teeth at the landings

HowStuffWorks 'How Escalators Work' / Designing Buildings Wiki 'Escalator components' / US patent class 198/331 'means synchronizing the operation of the steps and a handrail': the handrail is a rubber (conveyor-belt-like) loop driven from the same main drive as the steps so it moves at the same speed

Wikipedia 'Wheaton station (Washington Metro)' / MyMCMedia 'Wheaton Metro Station Boasts Longest Escalator in the Western Hemisphere' / WTOP (2025) 'The longest Metro escalator' / WorldAtlas 'The longest escalator in America': Wheaton station (Maryland, Washington Metro) has escalators 230 feet long, the longest in the Western Hemisphere

lines.text: If you make a staircase move, the steps smash into the floor at the top.
lines.caps: If you make a | staircase move, | the steps smash | into the floor at the top.

lines.text: So, every escalator step is really a little cart with four wheels.
lines.caps: So, every escalator step | is really a little cart | with four wheels.

lines.text: The front wheels and the back wheels ride on two different tracks.
lines.caps: The front wheels | and the back wheels | ride on two different tracks.

lines.text: Those tracks keep every step level, even while the chain climbs.
lines.caps: Those tracks keep | every step level, | even while the chain climbs.

lines.text: On the slope, each step sits a bit higher than the last one, so you get stairs.
lines.caps: On the slope, | each step sits a bit higher | than the last one, | so you get stairs.

lines.text: Near the top, both tracks flatten out, and the stairs fold into a flat floor.
lines.caps: Near the top, | both tracks flatten out, | and the stairs fold | into a flat floor.

lines.text: But the end of a moving floor could still pinch a shoe.
lines.caps: But the end | of a moving floor | could still pinch a shoe.

lines.text: So, the steps have deep grooves, and a comb's teeth slide right into them.
lines.caps: So, the steps have | deep grooves, | and a comb's teeth | slide right into them.

lines.text: Then each step flips upside down and rides back underneath, in one endless loop.
lines.caps: Then each step | flips upside down | and rides back underneath, | in one endless loop.

lines.text: But your hand is on the handrail, so it can't fall behind the steps.
lines.caps: But your hand | is on the handrail, | so it can't fall | behind the steps.

lines.text: So, the handrail is a rubber loop, driven by the same machine, at the same speed.
lines.caps: So, the handrail | is a rubber loop, | driven by the same machine, | at the same speed.

lines.text: The longest ones in America, at Wheaton station near Washington, are two hundred thirty feet long.
lines.caps: The longest ones in America, | at Wheaton station | near Washington, | are 230 feet long.

lines.text: You see, an escalator is just a chain of little carts, going round and round.
lines.caps: You see, an escalator | is just a chain | of little carts, | going round and round.

lines.text: That's why the stairs vanish into the floor at the top.
lines.caps: That's why the stairs | vanish into the floor | at the top.
